title: Power-series presentation from sections of finite local quotients
statement: Let $B,C$ be commutative Noetherian local rings with specified residue field $l$, a field [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field]. Write $\mathfrak m_B,\mathfrak m_C$ for their unique maximal ideals, and assume both rings are complete for these ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $i:B\hookrightarrow C$ and $\rho:C\to B$ be local ring maps inducing the identity on $l$ and satisfying $\rho i=\mathrm{id}_B$, where local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Set $I=\ker\rho$. Let $r\geq0$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in I$ have images forming an $l$-basis of $I/\mathfrak m_CI$ (every class is a unique $l$-linear combination of those images). Put $S=B[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $S$ is Noetherian local, complete for $\mathfrak m_S=(\mathfrak m_B,X_1,\ldots,X_r)$, with residue field $l$. There is a unique continuous $B$-algebra map $\phi:S\to C$ sending $X_j$ to $x_j$, where $C$ is a $B$-algebra via $i$; continuity is for the respective maximal-ideal-adic topologies. This map is local, induces the identity on $l$, and for every $n\geq1$ induces a surjective map $\phi_n:S/\mathfrak m_S^n\to C/\mathfrak m_C^n$ between Artinian local rings with residue field $l$ (Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize). If for every sufficiently large $n$ there is a local ring map $\sigma_n:C/\mathfrak m_C^n\to S/\mathfrak m_S^n$ inducing the identity on $l$ and satisfying $\phi_n\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}_{C/\mathfrak m_C^n}$, then $\phi$ is an isomorphism of complete local $B$-algebras. The $\sigma_n$ need not be $B$-linear or compatible as $n$ varies.

source.place: Tag 06SG, lemma-power-series, statement and proof, including its canonical surjections and cotangent-space decompositions. The inverse hypothesis is stated as the right-inverse equation used in its proof; the printed statement says left inverse. Power-series completeness and Noetherianity are the ambient complete-local construction in this lemma.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Put $J=(X_1,\ldots,X_r)$ and $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m_BS+J$. The constant-term map followed by $B\to l$ has kernel $\mathfrak a$: partition the nonconstant monomials according to their first variable with positive exponent to express every zero-constant series as $\sum_jX_jF_j$. A series with unit constant term $b$ has inverse $b^{-1}\sum_{k\geq0}(-w)^k$, where $F=b(1+w)$ and $w\in J$; each coefficient involves only finitely many powers. Thus precisely the series outside $\mathfrak a$ are units, so $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S=\mathfrak a$ and residue field $l$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] with $\Lambda=B$ and $J=\mathfrak m_B$ proves maximal-ideal-adic completeness. Both completeness conventions say that the canonical map to the limit of the power quotients is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; the displayed series calculations use [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

proof.text: Every $c\in C$ decomposes uniquely as $i(\rho(c))+(c-i(\rho(c)))$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_C=i(\mathfrak m_B)\oplus I$, and multiplying gives $\mathfrak m_C^2=i(\mathfrak m_B^2)\oplus\mathfrak m_CI$: the remaining products are exactly $i(\mathfrak m_B)I+I^2=\mathfrak m_CI$. Thus $\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2\cong(\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2)\oplus(I/\mathfrak m_CI)$. For $S$ the same calculation with the constant-term retraction and kernel $J$ gives $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2\cong(\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2)\oplus l^r$: modulo $\mathfrak m_SJ=\mathfrak m_BJ+J^2$ a zero-constant series is exactly its linear coefficients modulo $\mathfrak m_B$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The induced map of cotangent spaces is the identity on the first summand and sends the standard basis of $l^r$ to the specified basis $[x_j]$. It is consequently an $l$-linear isomorphism, also for $r=0$.

proof.text: Apply the surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-graded-rigidity] to $\phi:S\to C$: both rings are complete Noetherian local, its residue map is the identity, and step 3 gives cotangent surjectivity. Hence $\phi$ is surjective. It therefore induces surjective maps $\phi_n:S/\mathfrak m_S^n\to C/\mathfrak m_C^n$ for every $n\geq1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local], applied separately to $S,C$ with $K$ the indicated power, these quotients are Artinian local with nilpotent maximal ideals. Their residue fields are $l$ by the successive quotient maps. For $n\geq2$, their cotangent spaces are canonically those in step 3, since $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq\mathfrak m^2$. Thus $\phi_n$ induces an isomorphism on cotangent spaces.

source.place: Tags 06GZ, lemma-surjective-cotangent-space, and 06SG, lemma-power-series, proof: the canonical surjections and n greater than 1

proof.text: Fix $n\geq2$ large enough that a section $\sigma_n$ exists. Differentiating the equation $\phi_n\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}$ on maximal ideals modulo their squares shows that the cotangent map of $\sigma_n$ is the inverse of the isomorphism induced by $\phi_n$; in particular it is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] both quotient rings are Noetherian. They are complete for their maximal ideals because those ideals are nilpotent: their inverse systems of power quotients are eventually constant [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. We can therefore apply the surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-graded-rigidity] to the local residue-preserving ring map $\sigma_n$. It is surjective; it is also injective by $\phi_n\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}$. It follows that $\phi_n$ is its inverse and is an isomorphism. This application involves only the marked residue field $l$, and requires no $B$-linearity of $\sigma_n$.

source.place: Tag 06SG, lemma-power-series, proof: applying Tag 06GZ to h_n; the inverse equation is written explicitly

proof.text: If $F\in\ker\phi$, step 5 implies $F\in\mathfrak m_S^n$ for every sufficiently large $n$. This implies membership in every power, and separation in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] gives $F=0$. Together with the surjectivity from step 4 this proves that $\phi$ is a $B$-algebra isomorphism. A ring isomorphism between local rings sends their unique maximal ideals onto each other, hence the inverse also preserves all their powers and is continuous. Thus it is an isomorphism of complete local $B$-algebras. The argument uses each section only at its own level and requires no compatibility between levels.

The item's statement agrees with 06SG hypothesis by hypothesis. The source's 'left inverse' is correctly read as phi_n sigma_n = id, since its proof uses that h_n is injective. Not requiring sigma_n to be B-linear makes the statement stronger, and the proof never uses linearity. Steps: (1) S is Noetherian by the power-series Noetherian leaf, local by the geometric-series inverse, and m_S-complete by complete-over-complete-base with Lambda=B, J=m_B. (2) phi comes from adic-evaluation with alpha=i and ideal m_C; the x_j lie in m_C because rho is local, and continuity and uniqueness are checked. (3) The decompositions m_C=i(m_B)+I and m_C^2=i(m_B^2)+m_C I, and J/(m_B J+J^2)=l^r, give the cotangent isomorphism; this is a correct elementary calculation. (4) The surjectivity clause of graded-rigidity applies, with all hypotheses checked, and the Artinian-quotient lemma with K=m^n, N=n. (5) cot(sigma_n) is the inverse of cot(phi_n); the quotients are Noetherian and complete because their maximal ideals are nilpotent; rigidity makes sigma_n surjective and phi_n sigma_n=id makes it injective, so phi_n is an isomorphism. (6) The kernel of phi lies in the intersection of all m_S^n, which is 0 by separatedness. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Edge cases: r=0, C=B[[t]], and C=l[e]/(e^2), where no section exists at n=3; mixed characteristic is fine. Duplicate search over 06SG and 06GZ found only the item's versal siblings and two field-k nodes; none is a duplicate and there is no cycle. There are no new nodes and no SGA citation. I accept the two declared tool uses (generic sk-thm-p1 power-series completeness and evaluation).
